title: Recover from an External-Service Outage Without a Retry Storm
summary: Build bounded retries, visible failed work, and a paced recovery process that can handle new arrivals while draining a backlog.
prerequisites: Understand asynchronous work and S15's idempotency rules.
Be able to distinguish a temporary network failure from invalid business input.
learningObjectives: Explain backoff, jitter, and a circuit breaker in practical terms.
Define controlled recovery and a measurable backlog-clearing plan.

sections.heading: Retries are additional load
body: The scheduling service becomes unavailable while Anna and Max continue creating permitted Pending requests. If every failure retries immediately, the system produces more requests precisely when the dependency has less capacity. This is a retry storm: repeated attempts amplify the original outage and can consume Salesforce resources as well.

Begin with failure classification. A malformed request missing a required vehicle key will not repair itself through repeated identical calls. A temporary connectivity failure might recover. A timeout is especially important because the remote system may have completed the operation before the response was lost. That attempt needs idempotency or reconciliation, not an assumption that nothing happened.

callouts.text: Retry only when another attempt has a plausible path to a different outcome.

sections.heading: Define a bounded policy
body: Backoff increases the delay between attempts. Jitter adds a controlled random spread so many workers do not retry at exactly the same instant. A retry bound limits the number of attempts or the total age of retryable work. These are policy choices to test against the service contract, not universal magic numbers.

The synthetic policy below separates temporary errors from validation failures and unknown outcomes. Its delays are example design values, not Salesforce scheduling guarantees. A worker should store a future eligibility time or use an appropriate supported scheduling mechanism; do not hold an Apex transaction open by busy-waiting for the delay.

A circuit breaker is a controlled decision to stop making normal calls to a dependency after evidence of sustained failure, then allow a small probe or limited recovery path. It protects the system from repeatedly attempting work that is very likely to fail. The design must still show users and operators what remains Pending.

callouts.text: Every retryable item needs an attempt count, last outcome, next eligible time, stable business key, and terminal handling.

codeBlocks.caption: Synthetic outage policy to review, not a platform default
codeBlocks.code:
Validation failure: stop automatic retry; request data correction
Temporary 5xx/network failure: bounded delayed attempts with jitter
Rate-limit response: honor documented guidance and reduce demand
Timeout after possible write: retry with stable idempotency key or reconcile
Attempt/age limit reached: Needs attention with a responsible owner
Recovery: probe first, then gradually increase throughput

sections.heading: Preserve failed work and make ownership clear
body: An error queue is a durable list of work requiring attention, sometimes called a dead-letter queue. It is not a place to hide records forever. Include a concise error category, the relevant business identifier, the last attempt, and the action required. Avoid storing unnecessary customer details or complete authentication-bearing requests.

Oleg should see the number and age of unresolved bookings, while the operator can distinguish data correction from dependency recovery. A retry button should not blindly assign a new operation identity. Reusing the same business key allows the service to recognize a previously completed reservation.

Specify what users may do while the dependency is down. If the approved product contract allows a Pending request, explain that no slot is yet confirmed. If the business requires immediate reservation, the interface must follow a different failure path. Queue design cannot override that product decision.

callouts.text: Moving failures into a queue does not make the customer outcome successful.

sections.heading: Recover at a controlled rate
body: After the dependency returns, do not release the entire backlog at once. First verify a small probe, then increase the allowed rate while watching errors, response time, and queue age. Capacity must handle both new requests and old work. If arrivals equal completions, the backlog does not shrink.

Use a tabletop model: 600 waiting items, 100 new items per minute, and a hypothetical recovered capacity of 120 completions per minute. The net drain is twenty per minute, so the model needs thirty minutes to clear the initial backlog, assuming those rates remain constant. This arithmetic is useful planning, not evidence of actual Salesforce or provider capacity.

A small exercise can simulate success, timeout, invalid input, and rate limitation without calling a live service. Record transitions and the total number of attempts. Verify that a permanent failure does not loop and that a duplicate recovery attempt does not produce another reservation.

callouts.text: Measure oldest pending age, useful completions, and unresolved terminal failures throughout recovery.

exercise.title: Write an outage and recovery state machine
exercise.brief: Design the statuses and transitions for scheduling requests during a synthetic thirty-minute outage.
steps: Define Pending, Retry eligible, In progress, Completed, and Needs attention with clear meanings.
Assign each supplied failure category to a transition and a responsible owner.
Specify bounded backoff and jitter without implementing an Apex wait loop.
Model the 600-item recovery example and identify the assumptions.
Run a local simulation or manual trace that includes a duplicate attempt and a permanent validation failure.
acceptance: No path retries forever without a bound or operator state.
Unknown outcomes preserve the same business operation identity.
The recovery calculation separates new arrivals from backlog drain and is labelled hypothetical.
exercise.stretch: Explain how a circuit breaker changes behavior when the provider fails again during recovery.

knowledgeCheck.question: Why add jitter?
knowledgeCheck.answer: It spreads retry timing so many failed requests do not return simultaneously and create another burst.

knowledgeCheck.question: What is the purpose of an error queue?
knowledgeCheck.answer: To preserve unresolved work with enough context and ownership to correct, reconcile, or deliberately abandon it under an approved policy.

knowledgeCheck.question: Why might a recovered worker fail to clear the backlog?
knowledgeCheck.answer: Its completion rate may only match or remain below the rate of new arrivals, leaving no spare capacity for old work.

recap: Bound attempts and preserve unresolved business work.
Recover gradually and observe net backlog drain.
